metadata.title: Hardening.
metadata.note: Weekly update (changelog framing). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. Three reliability fixes: (1) model ID consolidated into collector/models.py (GROQ_MODEL + GROQ_REASONING_EFFORT), imported by edgar_collector/news_collector/setup_check instead of hardcoded in 3 places; (2) the 10-K/A bug — get_filings(form='10-K') is a prefix match that also returns 10-K/A amendments, .latest() picked one with no Item 1 Business so extraction silently stored nothing (AMD extraction_ok:false); fixed to pick exact form=='10-K' (AMD FAILED→OK, NVDA & SNOW unchanged); (3) timeouts on all three external services — Postgres connect 10s/statement 30s, Neo4j connect 10s/retry ≤15s, Bedrock read 30s/connect 10s/bounded retries; previously only ArXiv had a timeout; verified via unroutable IP (gave up ~10s). All env-overridable. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B03 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW: figures from the creator's change log; specific retired-model string kept off-screen to avoid dating.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. Three fixes on the vendor-intel system this week, and they're all about the same thing: the system failing badly. A model ID copied into three files, a bug that silently stored nothing, and services that could hang forever. Let's make it fail better.

props.command: Three reliability fixes this week — what was failing, and how did I make it fail better?
output: 1 · a model ID in three files

beats.narration_text: First, one source of truth. The model ID was hardcoded in three separate files. So when Groq retired the model we were using, with no notice, both collectors broke at once, and fixing it meant editing the same string in three places. Now it lives in one file, models dot py, and it's env-overridable. A model ID is a dependency you can't pin, so the least it can do is live in one place.

card.title: One Source of Truth.
card.subtitle: stop hardcoding the model ID

items.quote: Groq retired it → both collectors down

card.caption: a model ID is a dependency you can't pin — so the least it can do is live in one place
card.footer: IMPORTED BY ALL 3 COLLECTORS · NOT HARDCODED

beats.narration_text: Second, a sneaky one. We fetch a company's annual report, the ten-K. But the lookup is a prefix match, so it also returns ten-K-slash-A amendments. And our code grabbed the latest filing, which was sometimes an amendment, and an amendment has no business section. So extraction silently returned nothing, and the row was stored as a failure. That's why AMD's data was empty. The fix: pick the exact ten-K. AMD went from failed to okay, and the others didn't change.

show.event: the before column builds: latest → amendment → nothing

card.title: The Silent Bug.
card.subtitle: a 10-K/A with no Item 1
card.caption: get_filings(“10-K”) is a prefix match — it also returns 10-K/A amendments
card.footer: AMD FAILED → OK · NVDA & SNOW UNCHANGED

beats.narration_text: Third, no more hanging. The whole codebase had exactly one timeout, on one HTTP call. Everything else, Postgres, Neo4j, Bedrock, could wait forever. One stalled service would freeze an entire brief. So I added connect and read timeouts to all three, with bounded retries. I tested it by pointing them at a dead IP: they gave up in about ten seconds, instead of hanging. All env-overridable.

show.event: the three service cards snap in

card.title: No More Hangs.
card.subtitle: a timeout on every external call
card.caption: everything else could hang indefinitely — one stalled service froze the whole brief
card.footer: UNROUTABLE IP: GAVE UP IN ~10s, NOT FOREVER

beats.narration_text: The theme of the week: fix it in one place, fail loudly instead of silently, and never hang. Three small changes, but they turn three different ways of failing quietly into failures you'd actually notice, and recover from.

artifactLines: Model ID now lives in one file (collector/models.py), imported by all three collectors — env-overridable.
The 10-K/A bug: .latest() grabbed an amendment with no Item 1, so extraction silently stored nothing — now it picks the exact 10-K (AMD: FAILED → OK).
Timeouts added to Postgres, Neo4j, and Bedrock — before, only ArXiv had one; everything else could hang forever.
Theme: fix it in one place, fail loudly instead of silently, and never hang.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Go find one external call in your code with no timeout, that's a hang waiting to happen. Then find one place you store a failure as if it succeeded, empty data marked okay. Those silent failures are the dangerous ones, because nothing ever tells you they happened.
